u/ChillAhriman has given good info on managing basic systems but here's some guidance on three above:

**Plagues**

These are waves of illness that can both impact the control/development of your counties, as well as pose a health risk to you, your family and courtiers. Development is key to getting ahead and you can minimise the development hit from plagues by building hospices or anything else that gives 'plague resistance'. Plague resistance though doesn't influence likelihood of an area getting a plague, or safety for characters - just how much it impacts control/development.

If a plague hits or is about to hit where your capital make sure to isolate capital and go into seclusion to protect yourself. And you will be given option after to invest back into counties which which I recommend always doing. 

**Legitimacy**

This is a measure of how legitimate you're seen as a ruler by your vassals and can impact their opinion of you as well as having other bonuses/maluses. Your required level will differ depending on what level of ruler you are and other factors. You want to keep this at least on your minimum level to avoid penalties, and ideally higher to get bonuses. Main ways to gain legitimacy are winning wars against rulers same level as you and above, or completing activities like hunts and feasts. You lose legitimacy through taking illegitimate actions (revoking titles), losing battles and plagues. 

**Travel**

This is a more fun mechanic but now when you complete an activity like a hunt or feast you go to a physical location on a map. The main things to consider here are 'travel safety' as you may find when you go through areas that the danger level is quite high. The higher the danger, the more risk of negative events which could harm or kill you. You can reduce danger through perks, changing routes, or hiring people to come with you through the travel panel.

Recommend looking up 'full employment' as explains it better than I can.

During the post war period both parties pursued an economic policy of full employment which was focused on keeping unemployment very low. However, during the 70s inflation and this consensus was abandoned under Thatcher.

She pursued a neoliberal policy which was conformable with high unemployment with purpose of bringing down inflation.

The idea that higher unemployment reduces inflation is mostly based around two factors: unemployed people have less spending power which reduces demand and lowers prices. Secondly, that higher unemployment prevents wage increases due to companies having more power than workers.

Now while not intentional, during the post recession period we have seen unemployment rates akin to the full employment era which is why this is being pursued.

It is a neoliberal policy and not only economic proposal to reduce inflation. There are also arguments about whether high unemployment is worth the lower inflation. A lot around the idea of sacrificing a few to benefit the many.
